title: Subtle Modal Verbs
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! Los verbos modales en C2 dejan de ser simples reglas de obligación o posibilidad para convertirse en herramientas de precisión diplomática y matiz emocional. Expresiones como 'needn't have' o 'might as well' demuestran un dominio superior del idioma.

parts.visual:
1. NEEDN'T HAVE vs DIDN'T NEED TO: 
- Needn't have + past participle: Hiciste algo que NO era necesario (te esforzaste en vano). 
Ej: You needn't have cooked; I already ordered pizza. (Cocinaste, pero no hacía falta). 
- Didn't need to + infinitive: No era necesario, así que probablemente NO lo hiciste (o es irrelevante si lo hiciste). 
Ej: I didn't need to cook because we went out for dinner. 

2. MIGHT / MAY AS WELL: 
- Significa que ya que no hay una alternativa mejor, 'bien podríamos' hacer algo. 
Ej: We've missed the last train, so we might as well walk.
parts.audio: Number 1: Needn't have versus Didn't need to. Use 'needn't have' plus past participle when you did something, but it was unnecessary. You wasted your effort. For example: You needn't have cooked; I already ordered pizza. You cooked, but it wasn't necessary. Use 'didn't need to' plus infinitive when it was not necessary, so you probably didn't do it. For example: I didn't need to cook because we went out for dinner. Number 2: Might or may as well. This means there is no better alternative, so we should do something. For example: We've missed the last train, so we might as well walk.

parts.visual:
3. DARE (Como verbo modal): 
- Usado principalmente en negativas y preguntas, sin 'to'. 
Ej: How dare you speak to me like that! (¿Cómo te atreves?) 
Ej: I daren't tell him the truth. (No me atrevo). 

4. SHOULD (Para coincidencia o probabilidad condicional): 
- Significa 'Si por casualidad...'. 
Ej: If you should see John, tell him to call me. 
Ej: Should you need any help, please contact us. (Inversión). 

5. WOULD (Para hábitos molestos en el pasado): 
Ej: He would always interrupt me during meetings. (Solía hacerlo y me molestaba).
parts.audio: Number 3: Dare, used as a modal verb. It is mainly used in negatives and questions, without 'to'. For example: How dare you speak to me like that! Or: I daren't tell him the truth. Number 4: Should, used for coincidence or conditional probability. It means 'If by chance'. For example: If you should see John, tell him to call me. Or inverted: Should you need any help, please contact us. Number 5: Would, used for annoying past habits. For example: He would always interrupt me during meetings. This implies he used to do it, and it was annoying.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el modal con el matiz correcto.

questions.question: I bought a lot of food, but my friends didn't come. I ____ so much food.
questions.explanation: Lo compró, pero fue en vano -> Needn't have + past participle.

questions.question: I ____ up early on Sunday because it was a holiday, so I slept until noon.
questions.explanation: No era necesario y NO lo hizo -> Didn't need to.

questions.question: Since the concert is cancelled and we are already dressed up, we ____ go to a fancy restaurant.
questions.explanation: Ya que estamos en esta situación, lo mejor es aprovechar -> Might as well.

questions.question: How ____ you say such a terrible thing to your mother!
If you ____ change your mind, let me know.
questions.explanation: If you should = Si de casualidad...

questions.question: ____ you have any questions, do not hesitate to contact me.
questions.explanation: Inversión condicional con should = Should you have...

questions.question: When we were kids, my brother ____ always steal my toys and hide them. (Hábito molesto).
questions.explanation: Would para hábitos repetitivos y molestos en el pasado.

questions.question: She brought an umbrella, but it didn't rain at all. She ____ an umbrella.
questions.explanation: Lo hizo, pero no hacía falta -> Needn't have brought.

questions.question: I don't know the answer, and I ____ ask the boss because he is very angry today. (No me atrevo).
You ____ worry about the tickets; I've already bought them. (No tienes necesidad, aún no has hecho nada).
questions.explanation: Needn't = no necesitas / no hace falta.

questions.question: We have to wait two hours for the next flight, so we ____ get a coffee.
questions.explanation: Might as well = podríamos (ya que no hay nada mejor que hacer).

questions.question: I ____ take a taxi because Sarah offered me a ride home. (No era necesario y no lo tomé).
He ____ always complain about the temperature in the office. It was so annoying!
If anyone ____ ask, tell them I'm in a meeting.
questions.explanation: If anyone should ask = si de casualidad alguien pregunta.

questions.question: You ____ paid for my dinner, but thank you very much! (Pagaste, pero no tenías que hacerlo).
Nobody ____ challenge the king's authority. (Nadie se atreve).
questions.explanation: Dares (aquí usado como verbo principal afirmativo).

questions.question: Since nobody else wants the last slice of pizza, I ____ eat it.
We ____ rush because the train was delayed anyway. We ran for nothing!
questions.explanation: Corrieron en vano -> Needn't have rushed (o solo needn't have si el verbo está omitido).

questions.question: ____ you require further information, please refer to the manual.
He was so terrifying that I ____ look him in the eye.

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe el verbo modal que falta.

questions.question: You ____ have cooked; I brought food. (No era necesario y lo hiciste)
I didn't ____ to go to work today. (No fue necesario y no fui)
We ____ as well stay here. (Podríamos - no hay alternativa)
How ____ you! (¡Cómo te atreves!)
____ you need help, call me. (Si de casualidad)
If he ____ call, tell him I'm out. (Si por si acaso)
He ____ always leave his socks on the floor. (Hábito molesto en el pasado)
I ____ not tell her. (No me atrevo - contracción informal daren't o palabra completa)
They ____ have worried; everything was fine. (Se preocuparon en vano)
We may as ____ leave now. (Igual podríamos)

pairs.target: Lo hiciste, pero fue en vano / no era necesario

pairs.source: You didn't need to do it
pairs.target: No era necesario (probablemente no lo hiciste)
Igual podríamos ir (ya que no hay nada mejor)
En caso de que necesites ayuda (formal)
Si de pura casualidad lo ves
Igual podríamos (sinónimo de might as well)
